args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in every production region (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate. (Its staging candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also marked unhealthy.) We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before deploying it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in every region and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) was unhealthy everywhere, with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0 now. The error rate is down to 0.2% and health checks pass.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 as a SEV2 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It says what failed, what I rolled back and the current state. It also says v2.3.1 shouldn't be deployed again until someone finds out why it failed.

The release history shows the staging version of v2.3.1 (v2.3.1-rc) was also marked unhealthy, but it was still deployed to production. That gap in the release process may be worth looking into.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
